findings: Frame-wait timeout is cleared before encoding; no encode timeout can leave idle unresolved.
No individual cancellation API; browser encoding itself is not cancellable.
submitFrame retains input reference until end-frame.
Detached metadata is not deeply frozen; the same object is exposed to callbacks and async code.
External copied event fires before encoding ownership flag; synchronous disposal may be followed by encoding.
Canvas-only omits DOM HUD, not canvas-rendered overlays.

requiredReceiverValidation: Fresh frame identity/camera/matrices/dimensions remain immutable across delayed encoding and consumer mutation.
No-frame and never-callback encode timeout; single-request cancel, synchronous callback disposal, late callback after new generation.
No overlapping encoder and bounded resources on rapid open/close/retry.
Real browser capture of active canvas without HUD, correct dimensions/orientation/postprocessing and no extra render or preserveDrawingBuffer change.
Document actual copy/encoding costs; no inherited GPU/FPS claim.
